prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Sentinel Vale: Earth-observation ground segment (planning, ops, processing, archive, access). Mission Control Center (MCC, alias Bluebell): real-time ops, anomaly response, releases validated commands, owns contact schedule and routing policy; contacts: readiness check, monitoring, post-pass closure; coordinates with PPF on mode changes, downlink priorities, gaps; sends operational constraints to MPS after anomalies/outages/config changes; end-of-shift record of open actions. Escalation: console lead, discipline lead, mission management if safety/continuity/recovery threatened. Flight Dynamics Facility (FDF, alias Mistral): orbit, maneuvers; sends orbit/visibility predictions, pointing products to planning. Payload Processing Facility (PPF, alias Forgehouse): processing, calibration, distribution; Primary/Backup Processing Clusters (failover tested; planning only checks capacity); archive transfers rate-limited during contacts; receives planning metadata from MPS (not a delivery commitment). Network Control System (alias Lantern): authoritative WAN status, station allocations, antenna readiness, contact times, timing alarm screening; sends MCC antenna status, link config, timing refs, routing readiness. Mission Planning System (MPS, alias Cedar): admits requests (User Services Portal/MCC) checking authority, target, timing, mode, volume, handling; builds draft schedule (imaging, recorder, housekeeping, S-band support; X-band downlinks for high volume); flags spacecraft/station/staffing conflicts; checks slew, sun-angle, power, thermal recovery, recorder, command load, separation; exports command preparation package to MCC command engineering. Command Validation Gateway (alias Osprey): validates syntax, timing, ranges, sequencing, mode, baseline consistency; rejects unapproved manual edits, missing provenance, expired config refs, activities outside planning authority window; executes authorized commands. Telemetry Ingest Service: validates frames, Pass Replay Packet, latest spacecraft state for command checks. Orbit Determination Engine: Doppler Residual Report per pass; orbital solution for events/visibility/geometry. Product Quality Service: quality planning feedback. Antennas: North S-Band (nominal uplink), South S-Band (alternate) to MCC; Kiruna, Svalbard X-Band to PPF. Actors: Spacecraft Operations Team (console lead, telemetry engineer, systems engineer): reviews late requests; coordinates with Flight Dynamics Team before orbit control; on fault preserve command state, no discretionary commanding; uses Antenna Deicing Notice for contingency margin. Flight Dynamics

New part:
S125: The Cybersecurity Desk reviews command preparation exceptions when unusual access, emergency procedure use, or nonstandard transfer paths are requested before uplink.
S126: Final approval requires concurrence from the Mission Control Center and the Spacecraft Operations Team before any command stack is placed in the queue for the next authorized uplink opportunity.
S127: After final command approval, orbit state management remains under continuous control so that operations users work from a common predicted trajectory.
S128: The Orbit Determination Engine fits dynamic orbit solutions using radiometric tracking, spacecraft telemetry timing, force models, and the latest approved maneuver history.
S129: Tracking arcs include measurements associated with the North S-Band Antenna, South S-Band Antenna, Kiruna X-Band Antenna, and Svalbard X-Band Antenna when those data meet quality and timing criteria.
S130: The Product Quality Service checks each orbit solution for frame consistency, covariance reasonableness, time-tag continuity, and agreement with recent contact predictions.
S131: The Flight Dynamics Team uses the residual report to separate station-related tracking biases from dynamic model errors before accepting an orbit solution.
S132: The Flight Dynamics Facility maintains the authoritative orbit catalog for the ground segment and records the modeling assumptions applied to each accepted solution.
S133: Maneuver screening evaluates orbit maintenance options against fuel use, ground contact visibility, payload outage constraints, and post-burn tracking opportunities.
S134: For each candidate burn, the Flight Dynamics Team computes expected state change, execution tolerance, recovery strategy, and the earliest time when the solution can be declared stable.
S135: Collision assessment uses externally supplied conjunction data together with the current covariance to estimate miss distance, encounter geometry, and probability of collision.
S136: The Flight Dynamics Team maintains screening rules that distinguish routine catalog monitoring from events requiring immediate operator notification.
S137: If the predicted risk exceeds the mission threshold, the Spacecraft Operations Team receives a maneuver recommendation package that includes timing constraints and operational impacts.
S138: Attitude geometry support translates the predicted orbit into Sun angle, Earth limb, lunar exclusion, target visibility, and antenna pointing information for daily operations.
S139: The Flight Dynamics Facility sends the Star Tracker Mask File after verifying predicted bright-object exclusions against the current attitude plan.
S140: Bluebell requires that each flight dynamics delivery include a validity interval, coordinate frame, generation time, and operational use statement.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
